tasks.short: Receive complaints, establish what happened, agree remedies and arrange follow-through.

steps.what: Register incoming complaints and link them to customers and orders.

loop.input: Complaint text and attachments, with customer and order lookup results.
loop.output: Complaint record with source references and unresolved fields.
loop.check: Validate identifiers against records; retain unmatched complaints without guessing their identity.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; unresolved fields enter the clerk's queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing forms handle structured submissions; free-text complaints require extracting facts from varied wording.

steps.what: Listen to the customer and clarify the problem and desired outcome.
Retrieve order terms, shipment events and previous contacts.
Ask the warehouse or service team to explain unresolved facts.
Choose a proposed remedy within delegated limits or seek an exception.
Explain the findings and proposed remedy to the customer.

loop.input: Verified findings, proposed remedy, approval limits and response template.
loop.output: Draft customer response with supporting record references.
loop.check: Check amounts and dates against records; clerk checks tone and commitments before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; disputed or sensitive exchanges return to a human conversation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover acknowledgements; explanations of disputed events require case-specific wording.

steps.what: Arrange the agreed credit, replacement or service correction and close the complaint.

tasks.design: Configure the {HELPDESK} to capture complaints from {EMAIL}, link evidence from the {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {CRM}, and route unanswered questions. A bounded loop drafts explanations; people handle difficult conversations and approve outgoing commitments and remedy instructions. The {WORKFLOW} routes remedies above delegated limits to the sales supervisor before release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Complaint evidence spans several systems. Disputed facts and remedy negotiations resist fixed scripts.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case workflows and integrations cover routing and records. Bounded extraction and drafting reduce paperwork; AI-assisted coding can reduce connector development effort.
tasks.still_hard: Establishing responsibility, winning back trust and securing operational follow-through remain human work. Poor shipment records limit useful automation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when the stated complaint hides a larger relationship problem and negotiate a credible remedy.

ambition.what: Weekly recurring-failure review with the fulfilment team

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time assembling evidence and chasing updates, with more time for difficult cases and recurring failures. Compensation limits and approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Review recurring complaints that threaten account retention.
reach.learn: Connect complaint patterns to account history, commercial exposure and practical recovery options.

evidence.claim: Knowledge-based answers, order lookups and escalation are available capabilities; negotiated remedies need separate controls.
Knowledge-based assistance can hand unresolved questions into a pre-filled request.
The step shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured complaint outcomes.

assumptions: This baseline covers written complaints plus telephone clarification, with an existing case queue.
Relationship work remains substantial despite the supplied automation prior.
GDPR applies to customer data. Access design includes retention and role permissions.
Access estimates include assessment of consultation under national rules; formal consultation may extend elapsed time.
Any later automated customer-facing conversational service must meet applicable EU AI Act transparency obligations.
unknowns: Complaint volumes, channels and proportion requiring negotiation.
Available order, shipment and customer-history interfaces.
Delegated remedy limits and required supervisor approvals.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing employee agreements.
research_questions: Which complaint categories can be resolved using existing records and approved remedies?
Does a case pilot reduce handling time without increasing repeat contacts or disputed commitments?
new_work: Review response drafts and unresolved customer or order matches.
Maintain remedy limits, routing rules and evidence mappings.
Monitor failed remedy instructions and reopened complaints.

tasks.short: Check requested products against stock, reservations and expected receipts.

steps.what: Read order lines and identify the requested product codes and quantities.
Look up physical stock by warehouse and stock status.
Check reservations, blocked stock and expected receipts to determine availability.
Ask the warehouse to resolve missing or contradictory stock information.
Record the availability result and unresolved shortages against the order.

tasks.design: Use existing availability rules in the {ERP} and stock feeds from the {OPS_SYSTEM} to populate each order automatically. Show stock status, reservations, expected receipts and data age together; route contradictions through the {WORKFLOW} to the warehouse. Keep inventory checks separate from stock reservation and customer delivery commitments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate stock and order screens require repeated lookups. Inconsistent reservation definitions and stale feeds undermine trust.
tasks.enabler_now: Standard availability configuration and stock interfaces often already exist. Small deterministic connectors and exception views can now be built with less development effort.
tasks.still_hard: Physical discrepancies, uncertain inbound dates and allocation disputes cannot be solved by reading records alone.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an unreliable stock position and obtain a credible operational answer before anyone promises delivery.
tasks.altitude: Routine lookups largely leave the clerk's week; shortages and unreliable stock receive attention. The clerk can prepare substitution options, while allocation and delivery-promise rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Suggest commercially acceptable substitutes for unavailable products.
reach.learn: Product compatibility, customer constraints and the limits of substitution authority.

evidence.claim: Order import and stock synchronisation are available standard capabilities.
Order-processing systems can check stock rules and route exceptions.
Availability arithmetic needs deterministic rules rather than a model; effort ranges depend on existing interfaces.

assumptions: Product codes are already captured in the order; reading and re-keying them for stock queries can disappear.
A typical distributor has stock records in the {ERP} or {OPS_SYSTEM}; no spreadsheet bridge is assumed.
This task determines availability and does not reserve stock or send a delivery promise.
Access estimates include checking consultation under national rules where work practices change.
GDPR applies where order-linked customer information is accessed; the calculation itself needs only product and quantity data.
unknowns: Which system is authoritative for physical stock, reservations and receipts.
Feed latency and treatment of blocked, quarantined or consignment stock.
Existing availability configuration and interface access.
Frequency and handling time of stock discrepancies.
research_questions: Can existing availability configuration cover the required warehouses and stock statuses?
How closely do displayed availability results match subsequent warehouse confirmation?
new_work: Investigate stale feeds and contradictory stock statuses.
Maintain warehouse mappings and availability rules.
Review shortage alternatives with the sales team.

tasks.short: Verify customer details and order lines against source documents, master records and previous orders.

steps.what: Read the customer order and identify details requiring verification.

loop.input: Customer order text or attachment and its source identifier.
loop.output: Structured order details linked to source passages.
loop.check: Validate required fields, units and identifiers; flag ambiguous lines for clerk review.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; unreadable or ambiguous orders go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use direct field mapping for structured orders; varied prose and document layouts need bounded extraction.

steps.what: Compare customer, address, product and quantity details with master records.
Check previous orders for duplicate references and inconsistent customer instructions.
Contact the customer to resolve missing details or conflicting instructions.
Confirm corrections and mark the order as verified.

tasks.design: Capture structured orders directly and use a bounded extraction loop for documents arriving through {EMAIL}. Deterministic checks compare fields with the {ERP} and {CRM}, detect duplicate references and show differences from previous orders. The clerk resolves uncertain instructions and approves corrections before the {ERP} marks the order verified.
tasks.previous_blocker: Order documents vary, while customer and product records sit in separate systems. Clerks compensate through repeated visual comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can produce structured fields with source references. Deterministic checks and a small exception screen can then handle most comparisons.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible historical match does not establish the customer's current intent. New delivery addresses, unusual units and conflicting instructions need clarification.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a legitimate change from a mistake and obtain an unambiguous customer instruction.
tasks.altitude: The clerk reviews highlighted discrepancies instead of comparing every field. They can help customers remove recurring submission errors; authority to change customer master records remains unchanged.

reach.task: Agree clearer ordering arrangements with customers who submit recurring errors.
reach.learn: Customer purchasing processes, account communication and how to agree usable order templates.

evidence.claim: Document-based order capture can check customer, stock and price rules, route exceptions and post to finance records.
A vendor case reports 70% touchless orders at allnex; that result does not establish this customer's achievable rate.
Historical comparisons can use deterministic rules; ambiguity about customer intent still requires clarification.

assumptions: The baseline includes document-based orders; structured orders bypass extraction.
Historical checks flag field changes and duplicate references rather than interpreting arbitrary free-text instructions.
Order corrections do not silently update customer master records.
GDPR applies to customer data; source documents and extracted fields need controlled access and retention.
Access estimates include assessment of consultation under national rules where work practices change.
unknowns: Structured-order share and common document formats.
Customer and product identifier quality across the {ERP} and {CRM}.
Which changes require customer confirmation or specialist approval.
research_questions: Which discrepancies currently cause downstream fulfilment errors?
Can extraction preserve product codes, units and quantities reliably across representative order formats?
new_work: Review ambiguous extracted fields and conflicting instructions.
Maintain validation rules, unit mappings and duplicate checks.
Sample passed orders for missed discrepancies.
Help recurring-error customers improve their order formats.

tasks.short: Calculate merchandise, service and shipping charges using agreed prices and applicable rules.

steps.what: Retrieve agreed prices, discounts and customer charging terms.
Check shipment weight, destination, service level and applicable freight tariff.
Calculate line amounts, discounts, shipping, applicable taxes and the total.
Obtain approval for nonstandard discounts, freight waivers or unclear commercial terms.
Save final charges against the order for confirmation and invoicing.

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP} to apply versioned prices, discounts, tax rules and rounding rules, with shipment inputs supplied by the {OPS_SYSTEM}. The {WORKFLOW} holds only pricing exceptions for sales manager approval and records the decision before charges are saved. No model is needed for the arithmetic or rule application.
tasks.previous_blocker: The arithmetic is already available in standard software. Manual effort persists where freight inputs, negotiated terms or exception approvals are disconnected.
tasks.enabler_now: Configuration and deterministic integration can connect those inputs. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort without changing how charges are calculated.
tasks.still_hard: Unclear contract terms, missing freight dimensions and specialist tax questions need accountable owners. Existing standard automation may leave little additional saving.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a technically correct charge conflicts with the commercial agreement and seek the right exception.
tasks.altitude: Routine charge preparation largely disappears, leaving commercial exceptions and tariff maintenance. The clerk can propose corrections to recurring freight leakage; discount and tax decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Review recurring freight waivers and discount exceptions.
reach.learn: Contribution margin, customer terms and evidence needed to change charging policy.

evidence.claim: Order-processing systems can check price rules and route exceptions.
Charge arithmetic, rounding and tariff application are deterministic work when approved rules and inputs exist.
The implementation ranges assume reusable standard calculation functions and accessible freight inputs.

assumptions: The baseline uses existing calculation screens; it does not assume clerks manually perform all arithmetic.
Pricing exceptions consume a time-weighted share across orders and do not occur on every order.
Approved customer terms and applicable tax treatments can be represented as explicit rules.
This task saves charges; sending an offer, confirmation or invoice is a separate action.
GDPR applies to customer-linked data. Access estimates include assessment of consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which charges the {ERP} already calculates automatically.
Availability of versioned tariffs, contract prices and shipment dimensions.
Required tax, currency and rounding treatments.
Commercial approval limits and frequency of pricing exceptions.
research_questions: Can existing configuration remove the remaining manual calculation triggers?
Do representative standard and exception orders reproduce approved totals, including rounding and freight thresholds?
new_work: Maintain effective dates for prices, tariffs and charging rules.
Resolve missing shipment inputs and unrepresentable contract terms.
Check calculation changes against approved example orders.
Review recurring freight undercharges and exception patterns.

role.altitude: The order clerk moves from repeated lookups and re-entry toward resolving uncertain orders, shortages and customer disputes. Commercial commitments, stock allocation and pricing exceptions retain their existing approval rights.
reach: Help wholesale sales representatives prepare feasible substitution options.
Support sales managers with recurring complaint and freight-exception evidence.
Help customers improve ordering formats and reduce avoidable clarification.
skills_to_grow: Interpret stock availability, reservations and shipment uncertainty.
Investigate discrepancies using linked source records.
Handle complaint conversations and negotiate within delegated limits.
Understand customer terms, freight rules and contribution margin.
Maintain validation rules and evaluate automation exceptions.
role.ambitious_version: Run a small order-assurance service that spots recurring customer submission errors, prepares shortage alternatives and brings evidence of fulfilment failures to sales and operations.
